conventions: numbers in quotes are exact rationals; unquoted numbers are decimal approximations

controls.title: Three conformers on the 4-cube, pair correlations
controls.question: Is the ensemble determined by the six pair correlations among all ensembles on the space?

expected.stability: every ensemble with pair correlations within tau (max norm) of the data has mass at most lambda_l1_norm * tau / gamma outside the support (Proposition E1.1)

controls.why: Any three conformers are determined by pair correlations (Proposition E9(a)); the answer does not depend on the weights.

controls.title: Five conformers on the 6-cube that form a face, pair correlations
controls.question: Is the ensemble determined by the fifteen pair correlations?
controls.why: The support is the exact ground-state set of a pair energy and its pair features are affinely independent (Theorem E1(a)).

controls.title: The square: one-body data do not see which sites move together
controls.question: Is the ensemble determined by the two one-body means (equivalently, by the laws of the two coordinates)?

expected.remark: with the observable x1*x2 added every ensemble on this space is determined (the four feature vectors are affinely independent)

controls.why: Two conformers and two coordinate laws: the smallest instance of the sharpness of the Renyi-Heppes count (Theorem E4).

controls.title: Exposed is not identified
controls.question: Is the ensemble determined by the mean of phi?

expected.trap: the support {a, b} IS the zero set of the non-negative function phi in the span; a tool that tests only this condition answers IDENTIFIED, wrongly: the features are not affinely independent on the support

controls.why: Condition (i) of Theorem E1(a) fails while condition (ii) holds.

controls.title: Four conformers on the 5-cube with a twin of the other parity
controls.question: Is the ensemble determined by the ten pair correlations?

expected.remark: three of the four conformers, with any weights, are determined (B1-01); the fourth breaks it

controls.why: A Hadamard quadruple on four of the sites (Proposition E9(b)); the cut polytope is 3-neighbourly and not 4-neighbourly.

controls.title: Two triangles: the laws of the three side lengths

space.description: triangles in the plane up to congruence, given by their side lengths (edges 01, 02, 12)

controls.question: Is the two-conformer ensemble determined by the three edge-length laws?
controls.why: The rigidity matroid of the triangle is free, hence disconnected: lengths of different conformers can be spliced (Theorem E5(b)).

controls.title: A globally rigid graph, individually generic conformers, a twin (the science division's Example D1)

space.description: four points in the plane up to congruence; all six distances measured (K4)

controls.question: Is the ensemble determined by the six edge-length laws?

expected.trap: K4 is generically globally rigid and the two conformers have no length in common, but the pair is not JOINTLY generic: in both, points 2 and 3 lie on a common line through which point 1 can be reflected

controls.why: Theorem E7 needs jointly generic conformers; this is the counterexample of the science division's review SCI-REV-0020.

controls.title: A shared rigid part: two mobile groups whose coupling the data do not see (Example D2)

space.description: five points in the plane up to congruence; all distances measured except 3-4

controls.question: Is the ensemble determined by the nine measured edge-length laws?

expected.what_is_determined: the positions of points 3 and 4 relative to the triangle 0-1-2, separately; not which position of 3 goes with which position of 4

controls.why: The graph is rigid, but the conformers share the triangle 0-1-2: the laws cannot see how the two motions are coupled.
controls.source: section 3.3 (Example D2), Problem O3; check R10

controls.title: Three states on a torus of two angles, all products of 1, cos, sin over the two angles

space.description: the torus of two angles (phi1, phi2)

names: means of u(phi1)*v(phi2), u, v in {1, cos, sin} (nine numbers)

controls.question: Is the ensemble determined by the nine means among all probability measures on the torus?

expected.remark: no three-state ensemble on this torus is determined by these data (Proposition E22); two states that differ in both angles are (Proposition E20')
expected.trap: a search restricted to a product grid of angles reports IDENTIFIED: the twin does not lie on the grid

controls.why: Every measure with the data lives on the circle where the bilinear form through the three states vanishes, and there the data are trigonometric moments of order at most two.
controls.source: section 4c.4 (Proposition E22; found by the internal review ER3)

controls.title: Two planar rigid bodies: a mirror pose for every number of legs

space.description: relative poses (rotation angle theta, translation t) of two rigid bodies in the plane; leg e joins the point U[e] of the first body to the point V[e] of the second (body coordinates), length |U[e] - R(theta) V[e] - t|

controls.question: Is the single pose determined by its six leg lengths?  (Four legs determine a generic pose in the plane.)

expected.trap: all attachment points of each body are collinear; then the reflected pose (-theta, (t_x, -t_y)) has the same length for every leg, for any number of legs, although the leg matroid is connected

controls.why: Theorem E7' is for generic attachment points; planar (here: collinear) bodies are excluded.  Connectivity of the matroid is not the whole criterion.
controls.source: section 3.3 (E7', 'What genericity excludes'); check P4; internal review ER2, F6

controls.title: A vertex of a regular 360-gon, means of (cos, sin)

space.description: the vertices (cos(2 pi k/360), sin(2 pi k/360)), k = 0..359

controls.question: (a) Is the conformation k = 0 determined by the two means?  (b) If each mean is known within tau, how much mass can be elsewhere?

expected.closed form: min(1, tau / gamma), gamma = 1 - cos(2 pi/360) = 1.523e-4: attained by the two neighbouring vertices

controls.why: The verdict IDENTIFIED is correct and nearly useless: an error of 1.5e-4 in one mean leaves the population of the conformation completely undetermined.  On a continuous circle the modulus is a square root (Example E1.2, Proposition E2.2).

controls.title: Identified, but not by the projection certificate

space.states: all sign vectors of length 8 with first sign +

observables.names: the 28 pair products x_i*x_j, i < j

controls.question: Is every ensemble on these four conformers determined by its pair correlations?

expected.must_abstain: a tool that only has the projection certificate ||x - Px||^2 (Theorem E10) must answer ABSTAIN or 'not certified by this certificate', never NOT_IDENTIFIED

controls.why: The span of the conformers contains another sign vector, so every positive semidefinite certificate vanishes there too; the support is nevertheless the exact ground-state set of a pair energy, which needs a certificate of degree at least 4 (the Complexity division's Proposition 13).  At n = 12, K = 9 this is the case for 92 % of random supports.

controls.title: One-body data on the 3-cube: the range of a pair correlation
controls.question: What is the range of E[x1*x2] over all ensembles with these three means?

dual certificates.upper: x1*x2 <= 1 + x1 - x2 on the cube, so E[x1*x2] <= 1 + m1 - m2
dual certificates.lower: x1*x2 >= -1 + x1 + x2 on the cube, so E[x1*x2] >= -1 + m1 + m2

controls.why: Nothing is identified here except the one-body means; the certified answer is an interval with a dual certificate for each end (Theorem E2(a) / E17(a)).

controls.title: The same data: the range of the population of one state
controls.question: What is the range of the population of the state +++?

expected.reading: the data are compatible with the state being absent and with a population of 35 %

controls.why: A certified restriction on a population when the ensemble is not identified.

controls.title: The same question with each mean known within 1/20
controls.question: What is the range of E[x1*x2] over all ensembles whose three means are within 1/20 of the data?

expected.dual certificates: the same two inequalities; each end moves by tau times the l1 norm (= 2) of its dual vector

controls.why: Bounded errors enter through the dual norm of the certificate (Theorem E2(a)).

controls.title: A frustrated known part: the thermal union bound fails

space.description: {+1,-1}^2; disagreement variables e_i = [x_i != +1]; states in the order e = 00, 01, 10, 11

model.envelope: d(x, y) = number of sites where x and y differ (slopes 1)

ensemble.member: mu proportional to pi * exp(-e1 + e2)

controls.question: Is TV(mu, mu*) at most the sum over sites of mu*(x_i = +) - mu(x_i = +)?

expected.trap: the bound is a theorem for product references and for positively associated polarised members; here the polarised member has Cov(e1, e2) < 0.  A tool must check the hypothesis (Proposition E15U) or abstain

controls.why: A violated bond can break the bound (Theorem E15T(d)).

controls.title: Product reference: the equality case of the thermal union bound

space.description: {+1,-1}^3, uniform reference, envelope = Hamming distance (slopes 1), centre +++

ensemble.member: the member most polarised towards -++ (it is in the class)

controls.question: How far, in total variation, can a member with these one-body populations be from the member polarised towards +++?

expected.formula: sum_i (sigma - mu(x_i = +)) = (sigma - (1 - sigma)) + 0 + 0 = 2 sigma - 1, sigma = 1/(1 + e^-1)

controls.why: Theorem E15(c), with equality for members polarised towards a centre one flip away.

controls.title: Two configurations, one noisy mean
controls.question: How well can the population p of state 1 be estimated from y, in the worst case over p?

expected.reading: at this noise level no estimator knows p to better than 0.335 in the worst case

controls.why: Theorem E17: the dual vector of the identified interval is a near-minimax estimator; lower constant sqrt(E sech^2(1+Z))/2.

controls.title: An unknown calibration factor destroys an identification
controls.question: (a) Is the ensemble determined by its two means?  (b) Is it determined if the two data are known only up to one common unknown positive factor?

(a).reason: nu(a) + nu(c) = 1/2, nu(b) + nu(c) = 1/2 and total mass 1 force nu(c) = 0

(b).reason: no combination of phi1, phi2 WITHOUT a constant term is non-negative with zero set {a, b}

expected.control: the ensemble concentrated on a IS determined up to the factor (certificate phi2)

controls.why: With an unknown factor the constant function leaves the span in which a certificate must be found (Proposition E23(b)).

controls.title: The length of a mean vector between its extremes determines nothing

space.description: the four corners (+-1, +-1) of a square; the observable is the position vector

names: the length |E Phi| of the mean position

controls.question: Is the ensemble determined by the length of its mean vector?  (Lengths range from 0 to sqrt 2.)

expected.what_is_determined: at length sqrt 2 a single corner (up to the symmetry of the square: four ensembles have it); at length 0 only that the mean vanishes
expected.remark: for a moment body of dimension at least two a length strictly between the least and the largest is shared by infinitely many mean vectors

controls.why: Theorem E25(b), (e).

controls.title: The least possible length of a mean vector identifies an ensemble

names: the length |E Phi| of the mean position

controls.question: (a) Is the ensemble determined by the length of its mean vector?  (b) If the length is known within tau, how much mass can be on the other two points, and how far can the weights move?

stability.mass off the support: at most r tau / gamma with r = sqrt(1/2), gamma = 3/2
stability.weights: the mean moves by at most sqrt(2 r tau + tau^2): a SQUARE ROOT of the error, attained along the segment between the two support points

controls.why: The length is at its minimum over all ensembles; Theorem E25(d).

controls.title: Squared means: consistency of the data is a partition problem

space.description: 2m configurations (i, +) and (i, -), i = 1..m; observable phi_i equals +A at (i, +), -A at (i, -), 0 elsewhere, A = a_1 + ... + a_m

controls.question: Is there any ensemble with these data?

instance 2.reason: 5, 4, 2 cannot be split into two parts of equal sum

expected.trap: a local fit of an ensemble to squared data can stall on instance 2 without proving anything; the certified answer enumerates signs (2^m linear programmes) or abstains

controls.why: Deciding consistency of squared-mean data is NP-complete (Theorem E26).
